objective: Proof. (i) The complement-invariant four-place knot relations (unions of antipodal pairs with full three-place projections) are exactly 30, in four classes under flips and permutations: parity (8 states), not-exactly-two (10), twelve (12), not-all-equal (14). (ii) A complement-invariant law can never pin a value: every piece's accepted relation is complement-invariant. (iii) Schaefer: only parity is tractable with unbounded occurrences. (iv) On plain systems only the eight relations excluding both constants can fail. (v) Census of failures of each signed class on every 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7.
status: Proved by FOUR-PLACE-20261031-001A-P001: the value-free four-place knots are 30 relations in four classes (parity 8 states, not-exactly-two 10, twelve 12, not-all-equal 14); none can pin (complement invariance is inherited by pieces); by Schaefer only parity is tractable; census over every signing of every 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7 (1, 1, 4, 14 systems): not-all-equal never fails, parity and not-exactly-two fail on every system, twelve on all but three with n = 7
title: The value-free four-place knots
